title: Seeking the start of a field sequence
statement: Let $k$ be a nonnegative integer, let $i<k$ index a work tape, and let $x$ be an input word. Let $ws$ be a finite list of nonempty words, and let $L$ be the sum of their lengths plus one per word. Consider a configuration $d$ in the running phase whose scanned cell on tape $i$ is nonblank. Suppose that for every integer $p$ with $-2\le p<L$, tape $i$ at position $d_i-L+p$ contains the symbol at position $p$ of the concatenation of the words in $ws$, with blank separators between consecutive words and blanks outside the concatenation. After $L+4$ steps, the seeking machine is in the done phase with tape head $i$ at $d_i-L$; it is not in the done phase at any earlier time. At every time up to and including $L+4$, the head on tape $i$ lies between $d_i-L-2$ and its initial position, inclusive, and every other work-tape head remains at its initial position.
hypotheses_covered: $i$ indexes one of the $k$ work tapes
The initial configuration is in the running phase
The scanned cell on tape $i$ is nonblank
Tape $i$ agrees with the specified concatenation-with-separators tape for every integer $p$ from $-2$ up to but excluding $L$
